Skip to main content

✦
MADE FOR PEOPLE-POWERED BUSINESSES

Your whole day,
beautifully run.

Manage appointments, walk-ins, clients, team schedules and recorded payments in one place.

Start your trial
Find your business
One live day
Bookings + walk-ins
Everything connected
Client to checkout
An editorial representation of a modern salon business. No customer relationship is implied.

THE DAY, SIMPLIFIED

Less admin between the moments that matter.

ClipperDesk keeps the working day connected in the background, so the experience out front can feel effortless.

BEFORE THE DOORS OPEN

Open ready.

Check appointments, staff availability and waiting clients before opening.

WHILE THE ROOM IS MOVING

Stay present.

Keep client preferences, schedules and appointment changes together.

WHEN THE LAST CLIENT LEAVES

Close clearly.

Record payments and review the day’s sales and services.

✦

One continuous record. Appointments, client history and recorded sales stay together.

See how the product connects

CALENDAR & FRONT DESK

The right appointment. With the right person.

See appointments, staff availability and walk-ins together. Reschedule or cancel appointments from the calendar.

Available staff, chairs and rooms
Calendar, walk-in queue and daily attention view
Reschedule, cancel or update an appointment
Explore calendar and walk-ins

CLIENT CONTEXT

Remember what matters to your clients.

Keep client history, preferences, forms and notes available to team members with permission.

Service and product history in one record
Preferences, allergies, forms and notes in context
Secure links for clients to manage appointments
Explore the client experience

CHECKOUT & REPORTING

Record payments. Understand your business.

Review services, products and totals at checkout. Record payments and issue receipts, then follow each sale in your reports.

Checkout totals and payment history
Recorded payment and refund adjustments
Revenue, stock and commission reports
Explore checkout and reporting

BUILT AROUND REAL BUSINESSES

Built for your kind of business.
Explore all 13 business types
Barbershops
Bookings, walk-ins and the chair plan in one view.
Salons
Multi-service visits and client context that travel together.
Nail salons
Technicians, stations and repeat client preferences.
Spa & sauna
Practitioners, rooms and treatment capacity kept aligned.
Fitness & recovery
Coaches, equipment and appointment-led sessions.
Pet grooming
Groomers, tables and every return visit in context.

A CONSIDERED WAY TO START

Set up the rules before opening the calendar.

Add your services, team and working hours. Set booking rules and preview your page before publishing.

Start your trial

About ClipperDesk

Manage appointments, client records, team schedules and checkout for beauty, wellness, fitness, health and pet-care businesses.

Built around the people who make each working day happen.

WHAT GUIDES THE PRODUCT

Our approach

01 · CONNECTED

One connected day

Keep appointments, client history and recorded sales together, so your team can follow each visit through the working day.

02 · CONSIDERED

Clear access and records

Business records stay separate, access follows each role, and times reflect the location. Financial corrections keep their history.

03 · CANDID

Clear expectations

See what each feature does and which tools your business will still need. Checkout records received payments, and specialist clinical and payroll systems remain separate.

CLARITY AS A COMPANY VALUE

Operator and contact

Clipperdesk operates ClipperDesk. Postal contact: 111 Galileo Dr, Stoney Creek, ON L8E 0B5, Canada.

Support and privacy requests: support@clipperdesk.com.

CALENDAR AND WALK-INS

Manage appointments and walk-ins together

Coordinate staff schedules, chairs and rooms, appointment changes and waiting clients.

OVERVIEW

The calendar brings scheduled visits, staff availability and walk-ins into one view.

YOUR WORKFLOW

How it works
01
See the day in useful views

View today, a day or week, or separate staff schedules. Filter by location, professional, service or status.

02
Update appointments

Reschedule appointments, assign staff, change services, mark no-shows or block time.

03
Fit walk-ins around appointments

See estimated waits and check staff and space before starting a walk-in service.

04
Recover from exceptions

Review appointments affected by late arrivals, delays, staff absences or closures.

What you can do
Appointment labels and icons show status alongside colour.
If someone else updates an appointment, review the latest version before saving.
Managers can approve policy exceptions but cannot double-book staff or space.
Important limits
Wait times are estimates and can change with service delays or staff availability.
Existing room and equipment requirements are checked where configured. The service editor does not provide advanced resource or treatment-layout editing.

Checkout and reporting

CHECKOUT AND REPORTING

Complete checkout and understand your reports

Record service payments, create receipts and trace report totals to the original sale.

OVERVIEW

Sales and payment records feed your revenue, stock, commission and tip reports.

YOUR WORKFLOW

How it works
01
Build checkout from the appointment

Review services, products, taxes, discounts, tips and any deposit before recording payment.

02
Record payments received

Record payments already received by cash, external card, bank transfer or another supported method. Record partial or split payments, or leave a balance to pay later.

03
Correct records while keeping their history

Payment adjustments retain the original transaction and the reason for the change.

04
Trace totals to their source

Use filters, printable reports and exports to review totals and their underlying records.

What you can do
Receipts and reports show the relevant currency and local time.
Product sales update stock; refunds record whether products are returned or written off.
Exports use your selected filters and include only records you can access.
Important limits
Checkout records payments received elsewhere. It does not charge cards or send refunds to a bank or card provider.
Inventory tools are limited; supplier purchasing and warehouse transfers are not available.

CHECKOUT AND REPORTING

Complete checkout and understand your reports

Record service payments, create receipts and trace report totals to the original sale.

OVERVIEW

Sales and payment records feed your revenue, stock, commission and tip reports.

YOUR WORKFLOW

How it works
01
Build checkout from the appointment

Review services, products, taxes, discounts, tips and any deposit before recording payment.

02
Record payments received

Record payments already received by cash, external card, bank transfer or another supported method. Record partial or split payments, or leave a balance to pay later.

03
Correct records while keeping their history

Payment adjustments retain the original transaction and the reason for the change.

04
Trace totals to their source

Use filters, printable reports and exports to review totals and their underlying records.

What you can do
Receipts and reports show the relevant currency and local time.
Product sales update stock; refunds record whether products are returned or written off.
Exports use your selected filters and include only records you can access.
Important limits
Checkout records payments received elsewhere. It does not charge cards or send refunds to a bank or card provider.
Inventory tools are limited; supplier purchasing and warehouse transfers are not available.

Skip to main content
Home

Resources

Set a clear booking policy

BOOKING POLICY

Set a clear booking policy

A useful booking policy tells clients what is reserved, what may be charged, when changes are allowed and how exceptions are handled. It should match the team’s actual operating process and receive appropriate legal review.

Published 2026-08-16 · Updated 2026-10-13 · ClipperDesk editorial team

A practical field guide for the working week.
01
Start with the operating decision

List which services, staff or lead times need special handling. Avoid copying a stricter policy that the team cannot apply consistently.

02
Put terms before confirmation

Show deposit amount, cancellation window and important exceptions before the client confirms—not only in a later reminder.

03
Preserve the accepted version

Keep the policy version and calculation attached to the appointment so a later edit does not rewrite an earlier agreement.

04
Design the exception path

Define who may waive a deposit or policy warning, which reason is recorded and how a refund or checkout correction remains traceable.

KEEP BESIDE YOU

Working checklist
Services and circumstances covered
Deposit calculation and due point
Cancellation/reschedule window
Late/no-show handling
Refund/waiver authority and reason
Client-visible contact or recovery path
Legal and operations approval date
This guide is general operating guidance, not legal advice. Online deposit collection is not currently available in ClipperDesk.

Set a clear booking policy

BOOKING POLICY

Set a clear booking policy

A useful booking policy tells clients what is reserved, what may be charged, when changes are allowed and how exceptions are handled. It should match the team’s actual operating process and receive appropriate legal review.

Published 2026-08-16 · Updated 2026-10-13 · ClipperDesk editorial team

A practical field guide for the working week.
01
Start with the operating decision

List which services, staff or lead times need special handling. Avoid copying a stricter policy that the team cannot apply consistently.

02
Put terms before confirmation

Show deposit amount, cancellation window and important exceptions before the client confirms—not only in a later reminder.

03
Preserve the accepted version

Keep the policy version and calculation attached to the appointment so a later edit does not rewrite an earlier agreement.

04
Design the exception path

Define who may waive a deposit or policy warning, which reason is recorded and how a refund or checkout correction remains traceable.

KEEP BESIDE YOU

Working checklist
Services and circumstances covered
Deposit calculation and due point
Cancellation/reschedule window
Late/no-show handling
Refund/waiver authority and reason
Client-visible contact or recovery path
Legal and operations approval date
This guide is general operating guidance, not legal advice. Online deposit collection is not currently available in ClipperDesk.

Security

SECURITY AND TRUST

How we protect your business data.

Control who can access your workspace, keep client attachments private and review important changes to your records.

Trust comes from careful stewardship and clear boundaries.

DATA AND ACCESS

Safeguards for your daily work.
Separate business records

Your business records are kept separate from other workspaces. Team members can access only the locations and records permitted by their role.

Account protection

Sign in with email and password or Google when enabled. Optional authenticator verification and recovery codes add protection to your account.

Private links and attachments

Appointment and form links expire and allow only their intended actions. Client photos and PDFs are restricted to authorised team members. Do not upload files from untrusted sources.

A history of important changes

Sensitive changes record who made them. Payment and refund adjustments keep the original transaction history.

Keep access appropriate

Use a separate account for each team member, review permissions and remove access when someone leaves. Collect only the client information your business needs. ClipperDesk does not claim an independent security certification or healthcare compliance.

Reporting and support

Contact support@clipperdesk.com with a security or privacy concern. Include an account or business reference and a brief description. Do not send passwords or sensitive client records.

See how ClipperDesk fits your business.

Keep client history together

KEEP CLIENT HISTORY TOGETHER

Keep client history together

Keep client visits, preferences, notes, forms, messages and purchases together, with sensitive information restricted to authorised team members.

A better day starts with the real operating problem.

AT A GLANCE

ClipperDesk connects each client’s visits, notes and purchases in one profile. Access permissions protect sensitive information, and your team reviews possible duplicates before combining profiles.

What the problem looks like
Preferences and formulas live in personal notes that the next authorised professional cannot find.
Duplicate profiles split visits and receipts across identities.
A contact update loses the earlier audit trail or weakens secure links.
Steps your team can take
01
Collect only useful context

Define why each field or note is needed, who can see it and how long it should remain.

02
Separate general from protected notes

Use narrower access for sensitivities, formulas, warnings and consultation evidence instead of sharing everything equally.

03
Match and merge conservatively

Reuse matching contact details and review linked records before merging possible duplicates.

04
Preserve requests and changes

Track consent, contact changes and privacy cases with authorship and deadlines rather than erasing the evidence.

How ClipperDesk helps
Step 1:
Open the business client profile from the appointment.
Step 2:
Review the visits, forms and notes you have permission to see.
Step 3:
Keep completed visits and their payment records in the client history.
Step 4:
Record contact changes, profile merges and privacy-request outcomes.
Limitations
Deletion and anonymisation requests can be reviewed, but final removal requires an approved retention policy.
ClipperDesk is not a medical-record system and does not claim healthcare regulatory compliance.

Manage walk-ins and appointments

MANAGE WALK-INS AND APPOINTMENTS

Manage walk-ins alongside appointments

Keep walk-ins visible, review estimated waits and check staff availability before starting service around existing appointments.

A better day starts with the real operating problem.

AT A GLANCE

Add arriving clients to the queue, then check staff availability before assigning a service. ClipperDesk keeps the queue alongside scheduled appointments, so your team can fit walk-ins around booked work.

What the problem looks like
A verbal queue estimate competes with the next booked client.
The team cannot tell why one walk-in moved ahead of another.
Actual waits disappear, leaving future estimates to guess.
Steps your team can take
01
Capture the request consistently

Record arrival, requested service, preferred or any qualified staff, and the client's notification choice.

02
Explain the queue order

Use a visible ordering reason and treat estimated start time as changeable operating guidance.

03
Check the real calendar before assignment

Confirm the service still fits around booked work and staff capacity at the moment of conversion.

04
Record how the visit ended

Record whether each client was served, cancelled, left or did not respond, along with their actual wait.

How ClipperDesk helps
Step 1:
Add a walk-in with service and staff preference.
Step 2:
Review estimated waits and the order of the queue.
Step 3:
Check availability before assigning staff and starting service.
Step 4:
Start service and preserve the queue-to-appointment history.
Limitations
A wait estimate is not a promise and should change when current work, staffing or service choice changes.
A walk-in cannot override a real staff or resource conflict; a manager may override policy warnings only.

Protect time with deposits

PROTECT TIME WITH DEPOSITS

Set clear deposit rules

Set deposit and cancellation rules, show clients the terms before confirmation and keep the agreed policy with their appointment.

A better day starts with the real operating problem.

AT A GLANCE

A deposit can help protect reserved time when the amount, due point, cancellation terms and refund handling are clear. ClipperDesk calculates deposit requirements and saves the policy shown at booking. Online deposit collection is not currently available; clients with a required deposit must contact your business. A deposit does not guarantee attendance.

What the problem looks like
Clients do not see the cancellation terms until after booking.
A policy edit appears to change an older appointment.
The front desk cannot trace a deposit into the final balance or refund.
Steps your team can take
01
Choose a proportionate rule

Decide which services require a deposit, how it is calculated and what happens after cancellation or no-show, with appropriate legal review.

02
Show the terms before consent

Present the amount and cancellation policy in the booking flow before confirmation rather than relying on a later message.

03
Preserve what was accepted

Save the policy and deposit requirement so future configuration edits do not rewrite the agreement.

04
Reconcile the money

Keep payment and adjustment records linked to the appointment so the team can explain any remaining balance.

How ClipperDesk helps
Step 1:
Use the business’s published booking policy.
Step 2:
Show the deposit amount before confirmation.
Step 3:
Direct clients to your business when a required deposit prevents online confirmation.
Step 4:
Review verified deposits at checkout and record payments received elsewhere.
Limitations
Online deposit collection is not currently available. A deposit-required booking cannot be confirmed online without verified payment.
ClipperDesk does not guarantee that deposits reduce no-shows or supply legal advice about cancellation terms.

Reduce scheduling conflicts

REDUCE SCHEDULING CONFLICTS

Avoid scheduling conflicts

Keep online and front-desk bookings aligned with current staff hours, service durations and availability, with a final check before confirmation.

A better day starts with the real operating problem.

AT A GLANCE

Scheduling conflicts are best reduced by making every booking path use the same working hours, staff eligibility, service duration and resource rules. ClipperDesk briefly holds a selected time and checks availability again before confirmation. Accurate setup still matters, and unexpected delays need your team’s attention.

What the problem looks like
A client sees a time the front desk believes is unavailable.
A room or piece of equipment is promised to two services.
A late edit silently overwrites a newer calendar change.
Steps your team can take
01
Write down the real constraints

Keep location hours, staff working intervals, breaks, service segments, cleanup time and required resource quantities current.

02
Use one booking path

Use the same availability checks for online bookings, front-desk appointments and rescheduling.

03
Recheck at the decision point

Check availability again when reserving and confirming a time, because another booking may have taken it.

04
Review changes to the working day

Record late arrivals, delays and staff absences so your team can identify affected appointments.

How ClipperDesk helps
Step 1:
Show available times for the selected services and qualified staff.
Step 2:
Reserve the selected time briefly while the client finishes booking.
Step 3:
Check availability and appointment changes again before saving.
Step 4:
Ask the team to review a changed appointment before updating it.
Limitations
Good configuration still matters: outdated hours, eligibility or resource quantities can make otherwise-correct results unhelpful.
Unexpected closures and service overruns require an explicit recovery decision; software cannot guarantee a conflict-free day.

TRUST AND LEGAL

Terms and Conditions

The proposed contract for accessing and using Clipperdesk, including account, subscription, client payment records, acceptable-use, data and termination terms.

1. Status, scope and important definitions

These proposed Terms and Conditions govern access to the Clipperdesk website, applications and related services (together, the Platform). They are a review draft and are not yet effective. The operator contact is listed below. Contract terms, governing law, notice handling and acceptance still require authorized review before these Terms take effect.

In these Terms:

Clipperdesk, we, us or our means Clipperdesk, the operator of the service;
Business Customer means a salon, barbershop or other appointment-led business that creates or uses a Clipperdesk workspace;
Authorized User means an owner, manager, receptionist, service professional, accountant or other person whom a Business Customer permits to use its workspace;
Salon Client means a person who books, receives or pays for a Business Customer's services or products; and
Customer Data means information submitted to or generated through a Business Customer's workspace, excluding Clipperdesk' own software, documentation and aggregated information that cannot reasonably identify a person or Business Customer.

The order form, pricing page, plan description, approved data-processing terms, refund policy and any written enterprise order accepted by both parties form part of the agreement. If those documents conflict, an approved signed order should control for its subject matter, followed by approved data-processing terms, these Terms, and then public product documentation. This priority still requires counsel approval.

1.1 What Clipperdesk provides

Clipperdesk is web-based appointment scheduling and service business management software. It helps Business Customers manage configuration, staff access, scheduling, public booking, client records and consent evidence, enabled client notifications, received-payment records, checkout, inventory and reporting. Available functions and limits depend on the current plan, configuration, permissions, provider availability and release status.

Clipperdesk is not a salon, barber, stylist, beautician, medical provider, accountant, tax adviser, payment card issuer or law firm. A Business Customer, not Clipperdesk, is responsible for the professional services and physical products it offers to Salon Clients.

2. Accounts, authority and access

An individual who registers for or administers a Business Customer account must have legal capacity to contract and authority to bind that Business Customer. The final age and capacity language requires jurisdiction-specific legal approval.

Business Customers and Authorized Users must:

provide accurate registration, billing and business information and keep it current;
protect passwords, recovery codes, secure links and devices, use multi-factor authentication where required, and promptly remove access that is no longer appropriate;
use named accounts rather than sharing credentials;
assign roles and permissions according to each person's actual duties; and
notify support@clipperdesk.com promptly of suspected unauthorized access.

The Business Customer is responsible for activity performed through its workspace except to the extent caused by a verified Platform security incident or as applicable law otherwise requires. Clipperdesk may rely on instructions from an authorized account owner or billing administrator.

3. Business Customer responsibilities

The Business Customer determines and is responsible for its services, availability, staff qualifications, resource capacity, pricing, taxes, discounts, cancellation and no-show rules, deposit terms, receipts, client communications, marketing choices, forms, consent wording, record retention and legal disclosures. The Business Customer must ensure those settings are accurate, fair, lawful, visible before commitment and consistent with its actual operations.

The Business Customer must obtain all rights, notices, permissions and consents needed for Customer Data, including sensitive notes, consultation information, images, attachments and marketing preferences. 6. Acceptable use

No person may use the Platform to:

break applicable law or another person's rights;
provide a prohibited, fraudulent, deceptive, unsafe or unlicensed service;
process payment for goods or services that the applicable payment provider does not permit;
upload malware, attempt card testing, probe security without written authorization, evade rate limits, or interfere with the Platform;
access another Business Customer's workspace or data without authorization;
send spam or marketing without the required consent and opt-out mechanism;
collect excessive or unlawfully obtained sensitive information;
scrape, resell, reverse engineer or copy the Platform except where law cannot restrict that activity; or
use automated access in a manner that creates unreasonable load or bypasses documented interfaces.

Clipperdesk may investigate suspected abuse and may restrict affected access where reasonably necessary to protect people, Business Customers, providers or the Platform. Emergency action should be proportionate, documented and followed by notice where lawful and safe.

7. Customer Data, privacy and confidentiality

As between Clipperdesk and the Business Customer, the Business Customer retains its rights in Customer Data. It grants Clipperdesk and approved service providers the limited rights needed to host, secure, transmit, back up, support and otherwise provide the Platform.

The roles of each party depend on the data and purpose. Clipperdesk expects to act as a service provider or processor for much of the salon client data a Business Customer controls, and as an independent controller or data fiduciary for account, security, subscription and direct website information. Those roles must be confirmed in the approved Privacy Policy and any data-processing agreement.

Each party must protect the other party's non-public business, technical and personal information using reasonable safeguards and use it only for the agreement, except where disclosure is authorized or legally required. Specific enterprise confidentiality, audit, subprocessor and breach-notification terms belong in an approved order or data-processing agreement.

7.1 Feedback and aggregated information

If a user voluntarily provides product feedback, Clipperdesk may use it to improve the Platform without identifying the contributor publicly. Clipperdesk may generate aggregated or de-identified operational information only where it cannot reasonably identify a person or Business Customer and may not reverse that protection.

8. Intellectual property

Clipperdesk and its licensors retain their rights in the Platform, brand, documentation and underlying technology. Subject to payment and these Terms, the Business Customer receives a limited, non-exclusive, non-transferable right for its Authorized Users to use the Platform during the subscription term for its internal business operations.

The Business Customer retains its rights in its names, marks, content and Customer Data. It authorizes Clipperdesk to display that material only as needed to provide its configured workspace and public booking experience. Neither party receives ownership of the other party's marks.

9. Third-party services

Clipperdesk includes optional Google Maps address-search, map and navigation features. Use of Google Maps features and content is subject to the then-current Google Maps End User Additional Terms of Service and Google Privacy Policy. Business Customers must review their public address, set accurate entrance details and provide arrival instructions where needed. Map navigation may end at a street or building rather than the precise entrance. Manual address entry and booking without customer geolocation remain available.

The Platform depends on Google for optional sign-in, Stripe for enabled payments, and configured email, SMS, hosting or infrastructure providers. See the Privacy Policy for the operating provider disclosures. Their availability, buyer terms and privacy practices may apply to the functions they perform. Clipperdesk must not materially expand a provider's use of Customer Data without the notice, contract and approval required by applicable law and the agreement.

Third-party integrations may be unavailable, delayed or rejected. The Platform must communicate known material failures honestly and must not treat a provider redirect or browser message as final payment or delivery evidence.

10. Security, availability and support

Clipperdesk uses documented tenant boundaries, role-based access, secure action links, protected storage and append-only evidence for specified sensitive operations. These controls reduce risk but do not guarantee that the Platform is error-free, uninterrupted or immune from attack. The Security page describes the available safeguards; it does not claim a certification or guaranteed uptime.

Contact support@clipperdesk.com for support or security concerns. This draft does not provide a service-level or response-time guarantee.

11. Suspension, cancellation and termination

The Business Customer may stop using the Platform and may cancel renewal using the billing controls available to an authorized owner. Clipperdesk may suspend or terminate access for material breach, unlawful or unsafe activity, non-payment, provider mandate, or a security risk, subject to notice and a reasonable opportunity to cure where appropriate and legally permitted.

Termination does not erase amounts properly due, prior payment evidence, rights that accrued before termination, or records that must be retained. The current product lifecycle provides a dated export-availability window of up to 30 days after subscription termination where the account remains eligible. This is not a promise to delete all Customer Data after 30 days. The final record-specific retention and anonymisation schedule remains under review. Requests are reviewed before any deletion is authorised.

12. Service disclaimers

The Platform supports business operations; it does not replace professional, legal, tax, accounting, employment, health or safety judgment. Availability searches, reminders, estimates, reports and exports depend on the information and configuration supplied by the Business Customer and should be reviewed for the intended use.

Any warranty disclaimer must preserve mandatory rights and must be approved for the launch market. This review draft intentionally does not invent a final "as-is" warranty, service level or remedy.

13. Liability, indemnities, governing law and disputes

Governing law, dispute procedures and liability terms remain under legal review. This draft is not an effective contract. Nothing in it excludes a right or remedy that applicable law does not permit the parties to exclude.

14. Changes, notices and complete agreement

The approved version must carry a version and effective date. Material changes should be notified through an approved account or direct channel before they take effect, and renewed acceptance should be collected where law or the nature of the change requires it. Continued use must not be treated as consent where an affirmative agreement is legally required.

An approved order and these Terms should form the complete agreement for the Platform and replace earlier proposals on the same subject. Failure to enforce a term once is not a permanent waiver. Invalid terms should be narrowed or removed without invalidating the rest where law allows. Neither party may assign the agreement except under the approved assignment clause.

15. Contact

Operator: Clipperdesk. Postal contact: 111 Galileo Dr, Stoney Creek, ON L8E 0B5, Canada. Support and privacy contact: support@clipperdesk.com. Separate legal-notice arrangements and the final contract remain subject to review. Business Customers can currently use authenticated billing and account controls; Salon Clients should use the salon contact details and secure appointment link supplied with their booking.

An effective version will state its approval status and effective date.

TRUST AND LEGAL

Privacy Policy

How Clipperdesk collects, uses, shares and retains account, booking and billing information, including Google Sign-In, and how to request privacy rights.

LAST UPDATED
October 13, 2026
VERSION
1.1

This privacy policy is under review and is not yet effective.

About this policy

Clipperdesk provides appointment scheduling and business management software for salons, barbershops and other service businesses. This Privacy Policy explains the personal information handled through our website, business accounts, booking pages and related services. It applies to business owners, administrators, staff, customers booking with a business, and website visitors.

Clipperdesk operates the service. Our operator, postal address and privacy contact are listed in Contact us. A business using Clipperdesk may also provide its own privacy notice for the services it offers. Please read that notice when booking or providing information to that business.

Our responsibilities and business customer records

Clipperdesk determines how information is used to operate our website, register and secure accounts, manage our subscriptions and meet our own legal obligations. For these activities, we act as the controller, or the equivalent responsible organization under applicable privacy law.

For appointment records, customer profiles, consultation forms, business messages and other records managed by a business, that business generally determines why the information is collected and how it is used. Clipperdesk processes those records on the business's instructions as its service provider or processor. The business is responsible for its collection notices, permissions and appropriate use of customer and staff information. Payment providers may also determine how they use information for their own fraud prevention and legal obligations.

Information we collect and its sources
Business owners and administrators

When you register or use an account, we collect your name, email address, business name, profile information you provide, and account and verification records. Password-based accounts store password hashes. Security settings may include two-factor authentication and recovery information. We keep business memberships, roles and permissions to control access.

Owners and administrators provide business contact details, addresses, locations, opening hours, services, prices, staff assignments, booking policies and other settings. Subscription records include plan and capacity choices, billing name and email, invoices, payment status and limited payment-method details supplied by the payment provider.

Staff and team members

Businesses provide staff names, contact details, profiles, service qualifications, roles, permissions, working hours, breaks, leave and appointment assignments. Where used, operational records also include commissions, tips and related adjustments. These records support scheduling, access control and business reporting; availability records are not necessarily attendance records.

Customers booking appointments

You or the business may provide your name, email address, mobile number, date of birth, service preferences, referral information and communication choices. We handle selected services and staff, appointment times and locations, booking history, waitlist requests, cancellations, rescheduling and no-show records. Information also comes from bookings, visits and transactions recorded by authorized staff or imported by the business.

Businesses using consultation forms and client records may collect answers, notes, allergies or sensitivities, treatment preferences, typed-signature evidence, consent wording and versions, timestamps, images and attachments. Some of this information can be sensitive or health-related. Provide only information needed for your service. Businesses must determine the appropriate legal basis and any additional consent needed for sensitive information. Clipperdesk is not an emergency service or an electronic medical record system.

Website, account activity and communications

We process session and request information, IP addresses, browser or device information, login activity, security events, error information and audit records to run and protect the service. Communication records can include recipient details, message content or template information, delivery status, provider references, replies and consent or suppression records. Information you send to our support or privacy contact is used to handle your request.

Other sources include Google when you choose Google Sign-In, Stripe for billing and transaction updates, and messaging providers for delivery information. These uses are described below.

Google Sign-In and Third-Party Authentication
Permissions and information received

Google Sign-In is optional; email and password sign-in is also available. When you choose Google Sign-In, Clipperdesk requests the openid, profile and email permissions. Google supplies your Google account identifier, name, email address and email-verification status. The profile response may also include your profile picture URL and other basic profile fields. Clipperdesk does not save or display the Google profile picture or use those other profile fields in this sign-in flow.

These permissions do not give Clipperdesk access to Gmail messages, Google Drive files, Google Calendar, contacts or other Google services. We do not receive your Google password.

How we use and store this information

We use your Google account identifier to recognize your linked Clipperdesk account and your verified email to authenticate you, register your account and prevent conflicting account links. If the verified email matches an existing Clipperdesk account without a different Google link, the accounts can be linked. An existing Google link identifies its Clipperdesk account on later sign-ins. The name is used to prefill registration and becomes your Clipperdesk profile name when registration is completed; you can edit the name before completion.

New users still provide a business name and complete registration. We store the Google identifier and provider name with the account link, and the name and email with your account. Google Sign-In preserves any two-factor challenge already configured for your account.

OAuth credentials returned during sign-in are used to obtain the authentication response. Clipperdesk does not persist Google OAuth access or refresh tokens. An unfinished Google registration has a ten-minute validity window in the server-side session. Expiry prevents completion of that registration; it is not a guarantee that all session or backup records are immediately erased.

Retention, sharing and limits on use

Google account links and account profile information are kept while needed to provide your account and authenticate access. Account closure or a privacy request is reviewed using the retention criteria in Retention and deletion. We do not have automatic deletion of every account-related record.

Hosting and storage providers may process the stored account information to operate Clipperdesk. Your account name and email may also be used for account emails, workspace membership and subscription billing when you use those features. Authorized administrators of your business can see the account information needed to manage team access. The Google account identifier is not sent to advertising providers or used as payment or messaging metadata in these integrations. Necessary security or legally required disclosures are described in Sharing and service providers.

We use Google authentication information for account access and the associated account operations described here. We do not sell it, use it for advertising, credit decisions or unrelated profiling, or use it to train generalized artificial intelligence models. Clipperdesk's use of information received from Google APIs is subject to the Google API Services User Data Policy, including Limited Use requirements where applicable.

Disconnecting Google and requesting deletion

You can remove Clipperdesk's connection through your Google Account connections settings. Revoking access stops future use of that authorization. It does not delete your Clipperdesk account, remove information already stored by Clipperdesk, end your subscription or sign you out of an existing Clipperdesk session. Choosing Google Sign-In again can authorize a new connection.

Clipperdesk does not currently offer a self-service Google unlink control. To request removal of your Google account link, account closure or deletion of account data, contact support@clipperdesk.com from your account email and specify your request. We verify identity and explain any records that must be retained. If you need to continue using your account without Google, use the email password-reset option to establish access before removing the connection.

Google Maps and location features

Business owners can search Google for their business or address and position a customer entrance pin. When you use address search or load an interactive map, Google receives the search text, map requests and browser/network information needed to provide that feature. Google handles these requests under its Privacy Policy. The use of Google Maps features is also subject to Google Maps End User Additional Terms.

Clipperdesk saves the business's reviewed address, Google Place ID, owner-positioned entrance coordinates and optional arrival/parking instructions. Appointment records keep the assigned branch details so a later branch edit does not change historical directions. Google search suggestions and returned place geometry remain temporary in the browser; we do not retain a Google business-profile catalogue, reviews or photos.

Customers may choose Use my location to order known branches by straight-line distance. Browser permission is requested only after that action. These coordinates stay in memory on the booking page and are not sent to Clipperdesk, added to booking state or stored in the customer's record. Booking also works without sharing location. Opening external navigation shares the selected destination with the chosen map provider.

How we use information

We use the information described above to:

Register and verify accounts, manage workspace access, and protect accounts against misuse.
Configure businesses, locations, services, staff, permissions and availability.
Create and manage appointments, waitlists, customer records, forms and consent records on the business's instructions.
Manage subscriptions, invoices, payment reconciliation, receipts, taxes and recorded refunds or adjustments.
Deliver account, security, billing and appointment messages, and record delivery or reply information where enabled.
Provide available exports and reports, handle support and privacy requests, investigate failures and maintain security and transaction history.
Comply with applicable law, resolve disputes and protect the service and the people using it.

Required fields are identified in the relevant form. Without necessary account or booking information, we may be unable to provide the requested service. Business marketing messages require the applicable permission; appointment or security messages serve separate operational purposes. Google sign-in authorization does not constitute consent to marketing.

Where EU or UK data protection law applies to our own processing, our grounds may include performing our contract with you or taking requested steps before a contract; legitimate interests in securing accounts, preventing abuse and maintaining reliable services; compliance with legal obligations; and consent where required for optional communications or other optional processing. You may object to processing based on legitimate interests or withdraw consent as applicable. Businesses determine the grounds for their own customer and staff records, including any additional condition required for sensitive data.

Payments and billing

Clipperdesk subscriptions: Stripe processes subscription payments and provides hosted checkout and billing management. We send billing contact information and transaction details needed for these services. We store subscription and invoice references, amounts, currencies, tax and payment status, credits or refund evidence, and limited payment-method descriptors such as type, last four digits and expiry where Stripe supplies them.

Appointment and business payments: These are separate from your business's Clipperdesk subscription. Businesses can record payments, deposits, receipts, taxes, refunds and adjustments in their records. Where an enabled payment flow uses Stripe, Stripe processes the payment details and Clipperdesk handles transaction identifiers, amounts, currency, status and related business or appointment information. Availability depends on the business and payment flow; a recorded payment or refund is not itself evidence that money was transferred by a provider. A booking page will identify any payment action actually available.

Clipperdesk does not store full card numbers, card security codes or online banking credentials entered into Stripe-hosted payment interfaces. Stripe also processes information for its own payment security and legal purposes under the Stripe Privacy Policy. For appointment charges and refunds, contact the business providing the service. For Clipperdesk subscription questions, contact us. See our Refund Policy for the separate policy and its current status.

Sharing and service providers

We disclose information for the purposes described in this policy to:

The business you work for or book with, and staff with the relevant access permissions, to provide and administer its services. Information the business publishes, such as its address, services and public staff profiles, is visible on its booking page.
Google, when you choose Google Sign-In, to complete authentication under Google's Privacy Policy.
Stripe, for enabled subscription or appointment payment functions described above.
Hosting and storage providers, to host the application, databases and files, and email or SMS delivery providers, to send enabled messages and return delivery information. Delivery providers receive the recipient address or number and the message details needed to deliver it. Provider use depends on the enabled service.
Authorized support personnel and professional advisers, where needed to handle support, security, accounting or legal matters. Business-record support access is restricted and recorded.
Authorities or other parties, where disclosure is required by law or needed to investigate abuse, establish or defend legal claims, or protect people's rights and safety.
Parties to a business transfer, where legally permitted and subject to appropriate confidentiality and applicable notice or consent requirements. Any additional restrictions on Google-derived data continue to apply.

The confirmed operating provider details are listed in Contact us. Installing an integration does not mean it processes your information. Business features use only their enabled delivery or payment services. Development-only and disabled integrations are not operating providers for your records.

Clipperdesk does not sell personal information or share it for cross-context behavioral advertising. The public website does not load advertising pixels, third-party marketing analytics, session replay or fingerprinting tools. Businesses remain responsible for their own uses of exported records and for separate services they operate outside Clipperdesk.

Cookies and website measurement

We use cookies and browser storage for sessions, authentication, request protection and interface preferences. Our website emits limited interaction events within the page for buttons and pricing controls; the current implementation does not send those events to an external analytics service or store them as advertising profiles. First-party onboarding and security records support account operation and investigation.

You can control cookies and storage in your browser. Blocking session or security cookies may prevent sign-in or other functions from working. There is currently no sale or advertising-sharing activity for an opt-out signal to stop. Adding non-essential tracking would require an updated notice and any applicable consent or opt-out controls before activation.

International processing

Our operator contact is in Canada. Your location, the business's location and the places where service providers process data can differ. Our confirmed processing locations are listed in Contact us. Data processed in another country may be subject to that country's laws and lawful government-access requests.

Applicable transfer requirements depend on the destination, our role and the relevant law. For a transfer subject to EU or UK restrictions, a valid transfer mechanism must be in place, such as an applicable adequacy decision or appropriate contractual safeguards, with any required assessment and additional protection. Contact us for information about the safeguards applicable to your data. We do not represent that every provider or country has an adequacy decision, certification or a specific transfer agreement.

Retention and deletion

We retain information according to its purpose, our relationship with you, business instructions and applicable legal obligations. Retention takes account of whether information is needed to provide the service, maintain accurate transaction or consent history, investigate security issues, resolve disputes or meet accounting and other legal requirements.

Account and Google authentication records: retained while needed to operate and secure your account, subject to review when closure, unlinking or deletion is requested.
Account login history: configured for routine cleanup after 180 days. Other security and audit records may remain where needed for the purposes described above; this is not a universal expiry period for all security records.
Business, staff and customer records: retained for the business's service and recordkeeping purposes. The business controls its collection and requests changes through available tools or assistance.
Invoices, payment adjustments, consent and audit evidence: may remain after other records are removed where needed for legal obligations, security, disputes or reliable historical records. These records are not silently rewritten when a subscription ends.
Exports: client privacy-export files are marked for a 30-day availability period and use short-lived download links. That marker is not a promise of automatic physical deletion. Subscription termination records an export-eligibility window of 30 days, subject to access permissions and available export functions. Request an export before ending service; no complete automatic business export is promised.
Backups and archives: we cannot promise immediate removal from every backup or archive. A request must be reviewed against the applicable storage, backup and legal-hold arrangements; we do not state an unverified backup expiry period.

Canceling a subscription ends or schedules the end of paid service under the billing terms. It does not erase customer records, close every user account or revoke Google access. Account closure and customer record deletion are separate requests.

The current customer-record deletion workflow records and reviews a request but does not automatically erase or anonymize the records. Complete automated account-data deletion and a record-by-record disposal schedule are not available. Contact us or the controlling business to request review and understand what can be removed, what must be retained and why. We do not promise immediate or permanent deletion across all records. Where deletion is legally required, a technical limitation does not remove that obligation.

Your choices and privacy rights

Contact support@clipperdesk.com for information we control, including registration, Google account links, account security and subscription records. Include your account email, the relevant business and the action you request. Do not send passwords, payment credentials or sensitive consultation details in your initial message. We may ask for proportionate information to verify your identity and authority before releasing or changing records.

For appointment history, consultation information and other records controlled by a business, contact that business first using its booking or service contact details. We can assist the business with available access, correction, export and consent-withdrawal functions. An available export may omit internal security information, staff notes or records requiring a separate review; contact the business for a complete assessment of your request.

Account holders can change available profile and security settings. A valid appointment management link allows the changes offered for that booking. Ask the business to change communication choices or use the unsubscribe control where provided. Withdrawing consent affects future consent-based processing and does not require removal of records supported by another lawful ground.

Depending on the law that applies, your rights may include:

EU and UK: access, correction, erasure, restriction, portability, objection, withdrawal of consent and a complaint to your competent supervisory authority. Contact us about our controller processing or the business about its customer records. You may contact the UK Information Commissioner's Office or find an EU authority through the European Data Protection Board.
United States: applicable state rights to know or access information, obtain a copy, correct it, request deletion, opt out of specified processing, and receive equal treatment for exercising rights. Authorized agent requests and appeals are handled where required by applicable law. California rights concerning sale, sharing or certain uses of sensitive information apply where the law covers the processing; our current service does not sell information or use it for behavioral advertising. Contact us to submit a request or appeal a decision.
Canada: access, correction, information about our practices, withdrawal of consent subject to applicable limits, and challenging compliance. Contact us with a concern; you may also contact the Office of the Privacy Commissioner of Canada or the relevant provincial privacy authority.
India: where the applicable provisions are in force and apply to the processing, rights may include information about personal-data processing, correction, completion, updating, erasure, consent withdrawal, grievance redressal and nomination. Contact us for a request or grievance and information about the applicable escalation process.

Rights depend on applicable law and may have exceptions. We assess requests individually and respond within applicable legal time limits. We do not charge for or discriminate against lawful requests except where a permitted fee or other exception applies. No universal statutory deadline or compliance certification is claimed.

Security

We use account verification, permission checks, business-scoped access controls, expiring protected links and audit records. Specified sensitive client fields are encrypted by the application and private client attachments require authorized access. These safeguards do not imply that every field is separately encrypted or that any certification has been obtained.

No online service can guarantee absolute security. Our Security page describes current safeguards and their limitations. Protect your sign-in details, use available two-factor authentication and contact us about suspected account misuse. Businesses should restrict staff access to the information needed for their work.

Children and young people

Clipperdesk business accounts are for people with legal capacity and authority to act for a business. The service is not directed at children. A business may provide services to minors and collect related appointment or guardian information; it must give appropriate notices and obtain legally required parental or guardian permission. Contact the business or us if you believe a child's information was collected improperly. We do not use children's information for targeted advertising.

Changes to this policy

The version, last-updated date and effective date are shown at the top of this policy. We will update the notice when our practices change. Material changes will be communicated as required by applicable law, and new consent will be requested where required before information is used for a new consent-based purpose.

Contact us

For privacy requests, Google account unlinking or deletion requests, and concerns about information Clipperdesk controls:

Clipperdesk
111 Galileo Dr, Stoney Creek, ON L8E 0B5, Canada
Email: support@clipperdesk.com

For customer information controlled by a business using Clipperdesk, contact that business using the contact details on its booking page or service records.

Other sources include Google when you choose Google Sign-In, Stripe for billing and transaction updates, and messaging providers for delivery information. These uses are described below.

Google Sign-In and Third-Party Authentication
Permissions and information received

Google Sign-In is optional; email and password sign-in is also available. When you choose Google Sign-In, Clipperdesk requests the openid, profile and email permissions. Google supplies your Google account identifier, name, email address and email-verification status. The profile response may also include your profile picture URL and other basic profile fields. Clipperdesk does not save or display the Google profile picture or use those other profile fields in this sign-in flow.

These permissions do not give Clipperdesk access to Gmail messages, Google Drive files, Google Calendar, contacts or other Google services. We do not receive your Google password.

How we use and store this information

We use your Google account identifier to recognize your linked Clipperdesk account and your verified email to authenticate you, register your account and prevent conflicting account links. If the verified email matches an existing Clipperdesk account without a different Google link, the accounts can be linked. An existing Google link identifies its Clipperdesk account on later sign-ins. The name is used to prefill registration and becomes your Clipperdesk profile name when registration is completed; you can edit the name before completion.

New users still provide a business name and complete registration. We store the Google identifier and provider name with the account link, and the name and email with your account. Google Sign-In preserves any two-factor challenge already configured for your account.

OAuth credentials returned during sign-in are used to obtain the authentication response. Clipperdesk does not persist Google OAuth access or refresh tokens. An unfinished Google registration has a ten-minute validity window in the server-side session. Expiry prevents completion of that registration; it is not a guarantee that all session or backup records are immediately erased.

Retention, sharing and limits on use

Google account links and account profile information are kept while needed to provide your account and authenticate access. Account closure or a privacy request is reviewed using the retention criteria in Retention and deletion. We do not have automatic deletion of every account-related record.

Hosting and storage providers may process the stored account information to operate Clipperdesk. Your account name and email may also be used for account emails, workspace membership and subscription billing when you use those features. Authorized administrators of your business can see the account information needed to manage team access. The Google account identifier is not sent to advertising providers or used as payment or messaging metadata in these integrations. Necessary security or legally required disclosures are described in Sharing and service providers.

We use Google authentication information for account access and the associated account operations described here. We do not sell it, use it for advertising, credit decisions or unrelated profiling, or use it to train generalized artificial intelligence models. Clipperdesk's use of information received from Google APIs is subject to the Google API Services User Data Policy, including Limited Use requirements where applicable.

Disconnecting Google and requesting deletion

Required fields are identified in the relevant form. Without necessary account or booking information, we may be unable to provide the requested service. We use account verification, permission checks, business-scoped access controls, expiring protected links and audit records. Children and young people

Clipperdesk business accounts are for people with legal capacity and authority to act for a business. The service is not directed at children. A business may provide services to minors and collect related appointment or guardian information; it must give appropriate notices and obtain legally required parental or guardian permission. Contact the business or us if you believe a child's information was collected improperly. We do not use children's information for targeted advertising.

The version, last-updated date and effective date are shown at the top of this policy. We will update the notice when our practices change. 111 Galileo Dr, Stoney Creek, ON L8E 0B5, Canada

Canceling a subscription ends or schedules the end of paid service under the billing terms. It does not erase customer records, close every user account or revoke Google access. Account closure and customer record deletion are separate requests.

The current customer-record deletion workflow records and reviews a request but does not automatically erase or anonymize the records. Complete automated account-data deletion and a record-by-record disposal schedule are not available. Contact us or the controlling business to request review and understand what can be removed, what must be retained and why. We do not promise immediate or permanent deletion across all records. Where deletion is legally required, a technical limitation does not remove that obligation.

Your choices and privacy rights

Contact support@clipperdesk.com for information we control, including registration, Google account links, account security and subscription records. Include your account email, the relevant business and the action you request. Do not send passwords, payment credentials or sensitive consultation details in your initial message. We may ask for proportionate information to verify your identity and authority before releasing or changing records.

For appointment history, consultation information and other records controlled by a business, contact that business first using its booking or service contact details. We can assist the business with available access, correction, export and consent-withdrawal functions. An available export may omit internal security information, staff notes or records requiring a separate review; contact the business for a complete assessment of your request.

Account holders can change available profile and security settings. A valid appointment management link allows the changes offered for that booking. Ask the business to change communication choices or use the unsubscribe control where provided. Withdrawing consent affects future consent-based processing and does not require removal of records supported by another lawful ground.

Depending on the law that applies, your rights may include:

EU and UK: access, correction, erasure, restriction, portability, objection, withdrawal of consent and a complaint to your competent supervisory authority. Contact us about our controller processing or the business about its customer records. You may contact the UK Information Commissioner's Office or find an EU authority through the European Data Protection Board.
United States: applicable state rights to know or access information, obtain a copy, correct it, request deletion, opt out of specified processing, and receive equal treatment for exercising rights. Authorized agent requests and appeals are handled where required by applicable law. California rights concerning sale, sharing or certain uses of sensitive information apply where the law covers the processing; our current service does not sell information or use it for behavioral advertising. Contact us to submit a request or appeal a decision.
Canada: access, correction, information about our practices, withdrawal of consent subject to applicable limits, and challenging compliance. Contact us with a concern; you may also contact the Office of the Privacy Commissioner of Canada or the relevant provincial privacy authority.
India: where the applicable provisions are in force and apply to the processing, rights may include information about personal-data processing, correction, completion, updating, erasure, consent withdrawal, grievance redressal and nomination. Contact us for a request or grievance and information about the applicable escalation process.

Rights depend on applicable law and may have exceptions. We assess requests individually and respond within applicable legal time limits. We do not charge for or discriminate against lawful requests except where a permitted fee or other exception applies. No universal statutory deadline or compliance certification is claimed.

Security

We use account verification, permission checks, business-scoped access controls, expiring protected links and audit records. Specified sensitive client fields are encrypted by the application and private client attachments require authorized access. These safeguards do not imply that every field is separately encrypted or that any certification has been obtained.

No online service can guarantee absolute security. Our Security page describes current safeguards and their limitations. Protect your sign-in details, use available two-factor authentication and contact us about suspected account misuse. Businesses should restrict staff access to the information needed for their work.

Children and young people

Clipperdesk business accounts are for people with legal capacity and authority to act for a business. The service is not directed at children. A business may provide services to minors and collect related appointment or guardian information; it must give appropriate notices and obtain legally required parental or guardian permission. Contact the business or us if you believe a child's information was collected improperly. We do not use children's information for targeted advertising.

Changes to this policy

The version, last-updated date and effective date are shown at the top of this policy. We will update the notice when our practices change. Material changes will be communicated as required by applicable law, and new consent will be requested where required before information is used for a new consent-based purpose.

For privacy requests, Google account unlinking or deletion requests, and concerns about information Clipperdesk controls:

Clipperdesk
111 Galileo Dr, Stoney Creek, ON L8E 0B5, Canada
Email: support@clipperdesk.com

TRUST AND LEGAL

Refund, Return and Cancellation Policy

The proposed refund and cancellation framework for Clipperdesk subscriptions and, separately, client appointments and payments recorded in the platform.

Print or save as PDF

Under review — not yet effective

This document is under review and is not yet effective. An approved version will state its effective date.

VERSION
0.3-review
LAST REVIEWED
13 October 2026
EFFECTIVE DATE
Not yet effective
REVIEW STATUS
Under legal and billing review
ON THIS PAGE
Status and scope
Clipperdesk subscriptions
Appointments and deposits
Eligibility
How to request
Processing times
Returns and delivery
Disputes and safeguards

1. Status, scope and payment roles

This proposed Refund, Return and Cancellation Policy is a review draft and is not yet effective. Refund eligibility and service timelines remain under review. Operator: Clipperdesk. Postal contact: 111 Galileo Dr, Stoney Creek, ON L8E 0B5, Canada. Support and privacy contact: support@clipperdesk.com.

Clipperdesk has two separate payment contexts. They must not be confused:

Payment	Seller or service provider	Current payment role	Policy that controls
Clipperdesk software subscription	Clipperdesk supplies the software; contact details are listed above	Stripe processes the subscription payment and hosts secure billing controls	The final approved Clipperdesk terms and refund policy, mandatory law and applicable Stripe payment-service terms
Salon appointment, deposit or in-person sale	The service business shown on the booking or receipt provides the service or product	Checkout records payments received elsewhere. Online deposit collection and provider refunds are not currently available	The Business Customer's displayed booking/cancellation policy, mandatory law and the applicable payment-provider rules

Clipperdesk does not ship physical goods. Retail products recorded in Clipperdesk are presently sold and fulfilled by the Business Customer in person unless that Business Customer separately publishes an approved delivery policy.

Nothing in this draft limits a refund, cancellation, withdrawal, chargeback or consumer right that applicable law does not permit the relevant seller or service provider to limit.

2. Clipperdesk subscription cancellations and refunds
2.1 Trial and first charge

A verified owner registration currently begins a 14-day trial and does not charge a payment method. A Business Customer reviews the plan, billing interval, currency, amount and applicable provider information before entering payment details. The trial does not charge automatically. A Business Customer must separately review and confirm a paid subscription.

2.2 Renewal and cancellation

Paid monthly or annual subscriptions renew automatically until cancelled. An authorized owner can use the Clipperdesk billing page or Stripe Customer Portal to schedule cancellation. Unless mandatory law or the checkout says otherwise, cancellation takes effect at the end of the current paid billing period and prevents the next renewal. Access continues until that date, subject to payment, security and acceptable-use restrictions.

Cancelling renewal does not automatically refund the current billing period. An approved refund may end access to the refunded product or period.

2.3 Subscription refund requests

The approved Clipperdesk operator is responsible for the proposed subscription refund policy and decision; Stripe processes the payment and any provider-backed refund submitted by that operator. A Business Customer may review invoices and billing controls in the Stripe Customer Portal and may use an approved Clipperdesk billing-support path. Questions can be sent to support@clipperdesk.com; this contact does not create an automatic refund entitlement.

Eligibility is determined by the Clipperdesk commitment shown at purchase, the final approved policy and mandatory law. This draft does not create an automatic refund entitlement or guarantee.

3. Salon appointments, deposits and sale cancellations

The service business shown on the booking page is responsible for the appointment, professional service, in-person product, cancellation decision and client support. Before payment, its Clipperdesk booking journey is designed to show:

the salon, selected service and location;
the amount and ISO currency;
whether a deposit is required and how it is calculated;
the free-cancellation cutoff, deposit refundability, cancellation fee and no-show fee configured by that Business Customer; and
links to the Business Customer's own terms and privacy notice.

The exact policy shown and accepted at booking is retained with the appointment and controls the normal refund decision. A later policy change must not retroactively reduce the rights shown for that transaction.

Where permitted by the displayed policy, a deposit may be applied to the final sale, transferred to an approved replacement appointment, refunded, forfeited against an applicable cancellation/no-show rule, or converted to an approved credit. Its total value must not be allocated more than once.

4. Proposed appointment-payment eligibility rules

Subject to the Business Customer's displayed policy and mandatory law, a full or partial refund should be approved when:

the Business Customer cancels and cannot provide a reasonable replacement;
a cancellation is made before the displayed cutoff and the accepted deposit policy says the deposit is refundable;
the final amount is lower than the deposit and the excess is not validly transferred or accepted as credit;
a payment was duplicated, the amount or currency was incorrect, or the transaction was unauthorized after appropriate verification;
payment succeeded but the booking or sale could not be completed and the service cannot be recovered; or
applicable law or the payment provider requires the refund.

A refund is not normally automatic for:

a late cancellation or no-show where the accepted policy clearly permits a deposit forfeiture or fee;
a completed service or consumed in-person product merely because the client changed their mind;
the portion of a service or product already properly supplied; or
a request that cannot be matched to a transaction or safely verified.

These exclusions never override a mandatory remedy for a service or product that was not supplied, was materially misdescribed, was defective, or otherwise qualifies under applicable law. A manager waiver or exception must be reasoned and recorded; it must not erase the original transaction.

5. How to request a cancellation or refund
5.1 Salon Client request

Use the salon's contact details in the booking confirmation or receipt, or the purpose-bound secure appointment link supplied for that booking. Include only the booking reference, payment date, amount, reason and enough information to verify the request. Do not send a full card number, card security code, password or one-time banking code.

The Business Customer should confirm whether the appointment is cancelled, whether a refund is approved or declined, the approved amount, the policy basis and the provider reference when available. Cancellation of an appointment is not by itself evidence that money reached the client's account.

5.2 Clipperdesk subscription request

Use the authenticated Clipperdesk billing page or Stripe Customer Portal. An authorized Business Customer owner may review subscription state, invoices and provider controls there. Send billing-support questions to support@clipperdesk.com. Refund decision and submission responsibilities still require approval before this policy takes effect.

5.3 Information and decision timeline

Contact the responsible seller for the status of your request. Acknowledgment, decision and submission timelines are under review; this draft provides no response-time guarantee.

6. Processing and bank timelines

Ask the responsible merchant when an approved refund will be submitted to the payment provider. Refunds should be returned to the original payment method wherever the provider supports it. A different destination must not be used merely for convenience; if the original method cannot receive the refund, the merchant and provider must verify a safe, lawful alternative.

After Stripe accepts a card refund, the customer's bank or card issuer commonly shows the credit in approximately 5 to 10 business days. A very recent refund may appear as a reversal, meaning the original charge disappears instead of a separate credit appearing. Provider or bank failure can take longer to identify. Where available, the merchant should supply the refund reference so the customer can ask their bank to trace it.

For a Clipperdesk subscription, the final approved policy must state the operator's submission target and the expected Stripe and bank processing timeline without promising a guaranteed credit date.

These timeframes begin after approval and provider submission; they do not mean the credit is guaranteed to appear on a specific day. Weekends, bank holidays, payment method rules, issuer processing, fraud review, insufficient provider balance or a failed refund may affect delivery. The responsible merchant must track failed refunds and arrange an appropriate alternative where required.

7. Returns, exchanges, shipping and service delivery

Clipperdesk is a web-based software service. There is no physical Clipperdesk product to return and no Clipperdesk shipping or delivery charge. Subscription access is delivered electronically to the registered Business Customer account after the provider confirms the applicable trial or paid state.

Salon services are delivered at the location, date and time shown in the booking. In-person retail return, exchange, hygiene, opened-product and defect rules belong to the Business Customer and must be disclosed by that Business Customer before sale. Clipperdesk does not create a mail-return right or address for a salon's physical products.

8. Disputes, chargebacks and payment safeguards

Customers should first contact the responsible seller or service provider so it can investigate and honor the displayed policy. This does not waive a right to contact the payment provider, bank, card issuer, consumer authority or court.

Submitting both a refund request and a payment dispute can result in duplicate credits or delay. Tell the responsible merchant if a bank dispute is already open. The merchant should not retaliate for a good-faith complaint, submit misleading dispute evidence, or issue a second refund without checking the provider state.

Financial corrections remain linked to the original payment. Recording a refund in Clipperdesk does not send money to a bank or card provider; the responsible merchant must arrange the actual refund and confirm its status.

9. Policy status and changes

This policy remains under review and has no effective date. An approved version will state the operator’s refund terms and service timelines. Material changes must not retroactively reduce rights for a completed purchase. The policy shown when a purchase is confirmed should remain available with its transaction record.
